question.prompt: Mr. J left his entire estate to his wife, his daughter, his son, and the cook. His daughter and son got half the estate, sharing in the ratio of \(4\) to \(3.\) His wife got twice as much as the son. If the cook received a bequest of \(\$500,\) then the entire estate was:

solutions.explanation:
The ratio \(4:3\) lets us compare the bequests in equal-sized units before knowing their dollar values. Give the daughter \(4\) units and the son \(3\) units. Together they receive \(7\) units, which is half the estate. The other half is another \(7\) units, so the entire estate contains \(14\) units.

The wife receives twice the son's share, or \(2\times3=6\) units. Since the entire estate goes to these four people, the cook receives the remaining
\[
14-4-3-6=1\text{ unit}.
\]
This unit is worth \(\$500\), so the entire estate is
\[
14\times\$500=\$7000.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Measure the shares in equal units
